maya: FYI I uploaded a perfetto trace for the 03/13 21:34 tail spike that hit prod: https://perfetto.local/trace/0d9f3a (client->gateway->runtime spans visible). :eyes:
sam: thanks — can you paste the root span timings? want to see where the tail lives (gateway vs runtime).
maya: Gateway spans look fine (~12ms), runtime exec spans have a long queue/wait before kernel launch for some requests. p95 moved from 45ms->160ms.
sam: can you also attach the nsys capture? want to check GPU queueing and CPU->GPU handoff.
maya: attached nsys: /artifacts/nsys/2141598765-runtime-nsys.qdrep and a perfetto slice showing kernel queueing. Command I ran: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda -o runtime_nsys ./run_workload.sh`
cheng: I pulled the trace — kernel selection log shows we picked `matmul_sparse` for seq_len<=32 after commit abcd1234. I think that change raised launch setup on some models due to additional memcopy path.
tim: also noticed batcher change in the same window: `pad_to_power_of_two=True` (commit ff11aa). That increases small-batch padding which can change KV cache hit alignment.
maria: perfetto shows repeated KV cache evict events aligned right before the long kernel queue. looks like cache evictions trigger cold-path compile/prepare. snippet from trace notes: `KVCache::evict(0x7ff) -> runtime.prepare_kernel()`
perf-bot: Regression alert: e2e_lat_p95 increased by +220% on nightly load test at 2026-03-13T21:30Z. Test id: nightly-serve-42.
maya: I did a focused nvprof run on one slow request — timeline: CPU enqueues request, runtime batches, then 85ms idle before kernel launch, then 12ms kernel, then back. idle is GPU queueing + kernel selection overhead.
sam: do we have a stacktrace or nvtx markers around selection? need to verify if selection does heavy CPU work (memcpy, quant conv).
maya: yes NVTX markers show `select_kernel` 48ms on the slow path. here's the debug output I captured: ```[2026-03-13T21:33:12Z] select_kernel seq=16 model=vicuna-8b score_sparse=0.78 -> chosen=matmul_sparse prepare_ms=32 extra_copy_ms=16```
cheng: that matches the commit — we added a fallback copy for certain layouts. If batch padding changed, those fallbacks may trigger more often.
tim: action item: revert pad_to_power_of_two locally in a canary, and re-run perfetto + nsys to confirm delta. Maria, can you also run a trace with `KVCache.metrics=on` to capture eviction timestamps?
maria: will run a canary now on dedicated-qa (small load). I'll attach trace id when ready.
maya: to help triage, I made a quick filter in perfetto UI: `span.name == "runtime.exec" && span.dur > 50` — that isolates the problematic slices. saving that filter as `runtime-tail-50ms` for the team.
sam: thx. if revert nails it, we'll follow up with a targeted PR: 1) revert pad change, 2) short-term patch to skip extra memcpy for seq<=32 when layout is contiguous, 3) add unit/regression test for selection latency.
deploy-bot: rolling canary triggered: deploy/runtime@revert-pad-2141598765 -> dedicated-qa (1/3 hosts).
maria: canary traces started: perfetto ids -> 0d9f3b, 0d9f3c. early signal: p95 dropped from 160ms->52ms on canary host 1.
cheng: promising. I'll open a PR referencing abcd1234 and ff11aa with detailed bench results.
maya: TL;DR: tail spike caused by combo of kernel-selection fallback (extra memcpy) + batch padding change causing more fallbacks + KV cache evictions aligning with cold kernels. repro path and mitigation are clear.
sam: great work — next: collect more canary traces and merge the quick revert if numbers hold. :thumbsup:
